articles.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 Makes History Reaching One Light-Day From Earth
articles.summary: NASA’s Voyager 1 probe, humanity’s farthest-flying spacecraft, has reached one light-day from Earth, after more than 49 years of constant travel. A light-day is the distance light travels in 24 hours, equaling about 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). The spacecraft achieved the milestone at 2:16 a.m. PST (5:16 a.m. EST) Nov. 18. articles.title: ‘Perhaps we are safer not knowing’: a year after his death, Rob Reiner’s JFK assassination book is revealed
articles.summary: The late director worked with David Hoffman and Dick Russell on a book about his lifelong fascination with what really happened on 22 November 1963 On 8 December last year, the great director Rob Reiner signed off the prologue for Who Killed JFK? , his book written with David Hoffman and Dick Russell and based on his podcast with Soledad O’Brien. Describing a lifelong fascination with the assassination of John F Kennedy in Dallas on 22 November 1963, and what he saw as the vast conspiracy to cover up who really killed the 35th president, Reiner wrote: “Maybe, people don’t truly want an answer. Perhaps we are safer not knowing … Well, I’m done being safe.” Six days later, Reiner and his wife, Michelle Reiner, were stabbed to death in their home. Charged with murder, their son Nick Reiner has pleaded not guilty . Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘No publicist or manager in sight’: 80s Madonna, unseen and off-duty – in pictures
articles.summary: In Madonna Into the Groove: An Intimate Portrait of the Queen of Pop , photographer Ken Regan opens his archive from 1985 to show never-before-seen photographs of the musician. The 160-page hardback showcases Madonna at her most vibrant, captured on a February day in Los Angeles, with accompanying biographical text by journalist Tomás Mier. With the majority of images previously unpublished, the book is a behind-the-scenes look at an artist coming into the peak of her powers Continue reading...

articles.title: Jeff Buckley was a 90s indie darling. Now gen Z think he’s the ‘yearner final boss’
articles.summary: With his unguarded lyricism and earnest delivery, the late singer-songwriter is having a moment among a generation that fetishizes unrequited desire Sydney Tripoli has collected Jeff Buckley memorabilia since 2019. She keeps her collection of T-shirts, posters, vinyl and other merch celebrating the late singer-songwriter in what she affectionately calls her “Buckley box”. The 27-year-old scours eBay and resale sites for these pieces; lately she’s noticed the prices “skyrocket”. “During the pandemic, it was impossible to find Jeff Buckley shirts. Now they’re everywhere on Depop,” said Tripoli, who works as an actor in Los Angeles. “Now [my collection] is worth thousands of dollars.” Continue reading...
